chapterTitle: False Teachers and the God Who Knows How to Rescue
themeTitle: “The Lord Knows How to Deliver the Godly Out of Temptation”

scripture.text: But false prophets also arose among the people, as false teachers will also be among you, who will secretly bring in destructive heresies, denying even the Master who bought them, bringing on themselves swift destruction.
scripture.understanding: ἐγένοντο δὲ καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται ἐν τῷ λαῷ, “But false prophets also arose among the people” — ψευδοπροφήτης, contrasting with the true prophets of 1:19–21. ὡς καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν ἔσονται ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι, “as false teachers will also be among you” — inside the church. οἵτινες παρεισάξουσιν αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας, “who will secretly bring in destructive heresies” — παρεισάγω, to smuggle in alongside; αἵρεσις, a chosen opinion, a faction; ἀπώλεια, ruin. καὶ τὸν ἀγοράσαντα αὐτοὺς δεσπότην ἀρνούμενοι, “denying even the Master who bought them” — δεσπότης, the owner of slaves; ἀγοράζω, from the redeem family: to buy in the market-place. They deny with their lives the Lord whose purchase they claimed. Christians differ on how to read ‘bought’ here — whether Christ's death was for those who finally perish, or whether they only professed to be redeemed — but the verse's force is clear: they are traitors to the Master they named. ἐπάγοντες ἑαυτοῖς ταχινὴν ἀπώλειαν, “bringing on themselves swift destruction.”

scripture.text: Many will follow their immoral ways, and as a result, the way of the truth will be maligned.
scripture.understanding: καὶ πολλοὶ ἐξακολουθήσουσιν αὐτῶν ταῖς ἀσελγείαις, “Many will follow their immoral ways” — ἐξακολουθέω, the ‘follow’ of 1:16, where the apostles did not follow fables; here people follow sensuality. ἀσέλγεια, shameless sexual excess. δι᾽ οὓς ἡ ὁδὸς τῆς ἀληθείας βλασφημηθήσεται, “and as a result, the way of the truth will be maligned” — ὁδός, the Way, an early name for Christianity (Acts 9:2); βλασφημέω, to slander. Immoral teachers bring disgrace on Christ's name.

scripture.text: In covetousness they will exploit you with deceptive words: whose sentence now from of old doesn’t linger, and their destruction will not slumber.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ πλαστοῖς λόγοις ὑμᾶς ἐμπορεύσονται, “In covetousness they will exploit you with deceptive words” — πλεονεξία, greed, wanting more; πλαστός, moulded, fabricated (our word ‘plastic’); λόγος, from the word family: their words are manufactured. ἐμπορεύομαι, to trade in, the merchant's word of James 4:13: they treat believers as merchandise. οἷς τὸ κρίμα ἔκπαλαι οὐκ ἀργεῖ, “whose sentence now from of old doesn’t linger” — ἀργέω, to be idle: their judgement is not idle. καὶ ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει, “and their destruction will not slumber” — νυστάζω, from the sleep family: to nod off. Judgement is awake.

scripture.text: For if God didn’t spare angels when they sinned, but cast them down to Tartarus, and committed them to pits of darkness, to be reserved for judgment;
scripture.understanding: εἰ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς ἀγγέλων ἁμαρτησάντων οὐκ ἐφείσατο, “For if God didn’t spare angels when they sinned” — ἁμαρτάνω, from the sin family. Three examples of judgement follow, each with a rescue. ἀλλὰ σειραῖς ζόφου ταρταρώσας, “but cast them down to Tartarus” — ταρταρόω, to consign to Tartarus, the Greek name for the deepest pit of the underworld; Peter borrows it for the prison of fallen angels (Jude 6). σειραῖς or σιροῖς — manuscripts vary between ‘chains’ and ‘pits’; the WEB reads ‘pits of darkness’, ζόφος, thick gloom. παρέδωκεν εἰς κρίσιν τηρουμένους, “and committed them … to be reserved for judgment” — τηρέω, from the hold family: kept under guard.

scripture.text: and didn’t spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah with seven others, a preacher of righteousness, when he brought a flood on the world of the ungodly;
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἀρχαίου κόσμου οὐκ ἐφείσατο, “and didn’t spare the ancient world” — κόσμος, from the world family: the inhabited world of Noah's day. ἀλλὰ ὄγδοον Νῶε δικαιοσύνης κήρυκα ἐφύλαξεν, “but preserved Noah with seven others, a preacher of righteousness” — literally ‘Noah the eighth’; φυλάσσω, also from the hold family: to guard, as distinct from τηρέω in verse 4 — the angels are kept for judgement, Noah is guarded for life. κῆρυξ, a herald: Noah warned his generation. κατακλυσμὸν κόσμῳ ἀσεβῶν ἐπάξας, “when he brought a flood on the world of the ungodly” — ἀσεβής, from the godliness family.

scripture.text: and turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah into ashes, condemned them to destruction, having made them an example to those who would live in an ungodly way;
scripture.understanding: καὶ πόλεις Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρας τεφρώσας, “and turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah into ashes” — τεφρόω, to reduce to ash. καταστροφῇ κατέκρινεν, “condemned them to destruction” — κατακρίνω, to pass sentence. ὑπόδειγμα μελλόντων ἀσεβεῖν τεθεικώς, “having made them an example to those who would live in an ungodly way” — ὑπόδειγμα, from the pattern family: an example set up as a warning; ἀσεβέω, from the godliness family: to act without reverence for God. Jesus used the same examples (Luke 17:28–29).

scripture.text: and delivered righteous Lot, who was very distressed by the lustful life of the wicked
scripture.understanding: καὶ δίκαιον Λὼτ καταπονούμενον, “and delivered righteous Lot, who was very distressed” — καταπονέω, worn down, oppressed. ὑπὸ τῆς τῶν ἀθέσμων ἐν ἀσελγείᾳ ἀναστροφῆς, “by the lustful life of the wicked” — ἄθεσμος, lawless, without any moral boundary; ἀσέλγεια, as in verse 2. ἐρρύσατο, “delivered” — ῥύομαι, to rescue, snatch out of danger. Genesis shows Lot's weakness; Peter shows that God still counted him righteous and rescued him.

scripture.text: (for that righteous man dwelling among them, was tormented in his righteous soul from day to day with seeing and hearing lawless deeds):
scripture.understanding: “for that righteous man dwelling among them, was tormented in his righteous soul from day to day with seeing and hearing lawless deeds” — βλέμμα, from the see family: what he saw; ἀκοή, what he heard; ἐγκατοικέω, to live among; ψυχή, from the life family; ἄνομος, from the sin family: lawless; ἔργον, from the work family; βασανίζω, to torture, to rack. Living in a corrupt culture tormented Lot's conscience daily. Grief over sin is a mark of the righteous.

scripture.text: the Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment;
scripture.understanding: οἶδεν κύριος εὐσεβεῖς ἐκ πειρασμοῦ ῥύεσθαι, “the Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation” — εἴδω, from the know family; εὐσεβής, from the godliness family: the devout; πειρασμός, from the test family: trial, testing, pressure; ῥύομαι, as in verse 7. ἀδίκους δὲ εἰς ἡμέραν κρίσεως κολαζομένους τηρεῖν, “and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment” — τηρέω, from the hold family; κολάζω, to punish, to restrain. This is the point of the long sentence from verse 4: God rescues and God judges, and He knows how to do both.

scripture.text: but chiefly those who walk after the flesh in the lust of defilement, and despise authority. Daring, self-willed, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignitaries;
scripture.understanding: μάλιστα δὲ τοὺς ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ μιασμοῦ πορευομένους, “but chiefly those who walk after the flesh in the lust of defilement” — σάρξ; ἐπιθυμία; μιασμός, pollution. καὶ κυριότητος καταφρονοῦντας, “and despise authority” — κυριότης, from the power family: lordship, dominion (Ephesians 1:21), perhaps the Lord's own authority. τολμηταὶ αὐθάδεις, “Daring, self-willed” — τολμητής, reckless; αὐθάδης, self-pleasing, arrogant. δόξας οὐ τρέμουσιν βλασφημοῦντες, “they are not afraid to speak evil of dignitaries” — δόξα, ‘glorious ones’, probably angelic beings; τρέμω, to tremble.

scripture.text: whereas angels, though greater in might and power, don’t bring a railing judgment against them before the Lord.
scripture.understanding: ὅπου ἄγγελοι ἰσχύϊ καὶ δυνάμει μείζονες ὄντες, “whereas angels, though greater in might and power” — two words from the power family: ἰσχύς, inherent strength, and δύναμις, ability in action. οὐ φέρουσιν κατ᾽ αὐτῶν παρὰ κυρίῳ βλάσφημον κρίσιν, “don’t bring a railing judgment against them before the Lord” — βλάσφημος, abusive. Even mighty angels leave judgement to God (compare Jude 9). The false teachers have less power and less restraint.

scripture.text: But these, as unreasoning creatures, born natural animals to be taken and destroyed, speaking evil in matters about which they are ignorant, will in their destroying surely be destroyed,
scripture.understanding: οὗτοι δέ, ὡς ἄλογα ζῷα, “But these, as unreasoning creatures” — ἄλογος, without reason, the opposite of λόγος; ζῷον, an animal. γεγεννημένα φυσικὰ εἰς ἅλωσιν καὶ φθοράν, “born natural animals to be taken and destroyed” — γεννάω, from the birth family; φυσικός, by nature; ἅλωσις, capture. ἐν οἷς ἀγνοοῦσιν βλασφημοῦντες, “speaking evil in matters about which they are ignorant” — ἀγνοέω, not to know. ἐν τῇ φθορᾷ αὐτῶν καταφθαρήσονται, “will in their destroying surely be destroyed” — φθορά, corruption, the decay the believers escaped (1:4). They live like beasts and will die like them.

scripture.text: receiving the wages of unrighteousness; people who count it pleasure to revel in the daytime, spots and defects, reveling in their deceit while they feast with you;
scripture.understanding: κομιούμενοι μισθὸν ἀδικίας, “receiving the wages of unrighteousness” — μισθός, pay; ἀδικία, from the sin family: wrongdoing. ἡδονὴν ἡγούμενοι τὴν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τρυφήν, “people who count it pleasure to revel in the daytime” — ἡδονή, the ‘pleasures’ of James 4:1; τρυφή, luxurious living; ἡμέρα, from the time family: even pagans waited till night. σπίλοι καὶ μῶμοι, “spots and defects” — the exact opposite of Christ, the Lamb ‘without blemish or spot’ (1 Peter 1:19). ἐντρυφῶντες ἐν ταῖς ἀπάταις αὐτῶν, “reveling in their deceit” — ἀπάτη, deceit; some manuscripts read ἀγάπαις, ‘love feasts’ (Jude 12). συνευωχούμενοι ὑμῖν, “while they feast with you” — at the church's fellowship meals.

scripture.text: having eyes full of adultery, and who can’t cease from sin; enticing unsettled souls; having a heart trained in greed; children of cursing;
scripture.understanding: ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντες μεστοὺς μοιχαλίδος, “having eyes full of adultery” — every woman is seen as a possible conquest. καὶ ἀκαταπαύστους ἁμαρτίας, “and who can’t cease from sin” — ἀκατάπαυστος, unceasing; ἁμαρτία, from the sin family. δελεάζοντες ψυχὰς ἀστηρίκτους, “enticing unsettled souls” — δελεάζω, to bait a hook, the word of James 1:14; ἀστήρικτος, unstable, the opposite of the believers ‘established’ (στηρίζω) in 1:12; ψυχή, from the life family. καρδίαν γεγυμνασμένην πλεονεξίας ἔχοντες, “having a heart trained in greed” — γυμνάζω, from the discipline family: to train like an athlete. They are disciplined — in sin. κατάρας τέκνα, “children of cursing.”

scripture.text: forsaking the right way, they went astray, having followed the way of Balaam the son of Beor, who loved the wages of wrongdoing;
scripture.understanding: καταλιπόντες εὐθεῖαν ὁδόν, “forsaking the right way” — καταλείπω, to abandon; εὐθύς, straight. ἐπλανήθησαν, “they went astray” — πλανάω, the wandering of James 5:19. ἐξακολουθήσαντες τῇ ὁδῷ τοῦ Βαλαὰμ τοῦ Βοσόρ, “having followed the way of Balaam the son of Beor” — the prophet hired to curse Israel (Numbers 22–24), who then taught Moab to lead Israel into idolatry and immorality (Numbers 31:16; Revelation 2:14). ὃς μισθὸν ἀδικίας ἠγάπησεν, “who loved the wages of wrongdoing” — ἀγαπάω, from the love family, here turned to a wrong object; ἀδικία, from the sin family, as in verse 13. Greed for gain under religious cover.

scripture.text: but he was rebuked for his own disobedience. A mute donkey spoke with a man’s voice and stopped the madness of the prophet.
scripture.understanding: ἔλεγξιν δὲ ἔσχεν ἰδίας παρανομίας, “but he was rebuked for his own disobedience” — ἔλεγξις, from the discipline family: exposure, rebuke; παρανομία, from the sin family: acting against the law. ὑποζύγιον ἄφωνον ἐν ἀνθρώπου φωνῇ φθεγξάμενον, “A mute donkey spoke with a man’s voice” — ὑποζύγιον, a beast of burden; ἄφωνος, voiceless; φθέγγομαι, to utter. ἐκώλυσεν τὴν τοῦ προφήτου παραφρονίαν, “and stopped the madness of the prophet” — παραφρονία, insanity. The irony: a dumb animal saw what the greedy prophet could not, and spoke more sense than he did.

scripture.text: These are wells without water, clouds driven by a storm; for whom the blackness of darkness has been reserved forever.
scripture.understanding: οὗτοί εἰσιν πηγαὶ ἄνυδροι, “These are wells without water” — πηγή, a spring, the ‘spring’ of James 3:11; ἄνυδρος, dry: they promise refreshment and give none. νεφέλαι ὑπὸ λαίλαπος ἐλαυνόμεναι, “clouds driven by a storm” — clouds that promise rain to a thirsty farmer but are blown away. ἐλαύνω, the ‘driven’ of James 3:4. οἷς ὁ ζόφος τοῦ σκότους τετήρηται, “for whom the blackness of darkness has been reserved forever” — ζόφος, the gloom of verse 4; τηρέω, from the hold family, as for the angels; αἰών, in the time family and the world family.

scripture.text: For, uttering great swelling words of emptiness, they entice in the lusts of the flesh, by licentiousness, those who are indeed escaping from those who live in error;
scripture.understanding: ὑπέρογκα γὰρ ματαιότητος φθεγγόμενοι, “For, uttering great swelling words of emptiness” — ὑπέρογκος, inflated, bombastic; ματαιότης, emptiness, futility. They sound impressive and say nothing. δελεάζουσιν ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις σαρκὸς ἀσελγείαις, “they entice in the lusts of the flesh, by licentiousness” — δελεάζω, as in verse 14. τοὺς ὄντως ἀποφεύγοντας τοὺς ἐν πλάνῃ ἀναστρεφομένους, “those who are indeed escaping from those who live in error” — new believers just leaving paganism are the most vulnerable; πλάνη, the ‘error’ of James 5:20.

scripture.text: promising them liberty, while they themselves are bondservants of corruption; for a man is brought into bondage by whoever overcomes him.
scripture.understanding: ἐλευθερίαν αὐτοῖς ἐπαγγελλόμενοι, “promising them liberty” — ἐλευθερία, the freedom of James 1:25, here falsely offered as freedom from moral restraint. αὐτοὶ δοῦλοι ὑπάρχοντες τῆς φθορᾶς, “while they themselves are bondservants of corruption” — δοῦλος, from the servant family. ᾧ γάρ τις ἥττηται, τούτῳ δεδούλωται, “for a man is brought into bondage by whoever overcomes him” — ἡττάω, to be defeated; δουλόω, also from the servant family: to enslave. What you cannot say no to owns you (John 8:34).

scripture.text: For if, after they have escaped the defilement of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in it and overcome, the last state has become worse for them than the first.
scripture.understanding: εἰ γὰρ ἀποφυγόντες τὰ μιάσματα τοῦ κόσμου, “For if, after they have escaped the defilement of the world” — ἀποφεύγω, the ‘escaped’ of 1:4; μίασμα, stain; κόσμος, from the world family. ἐν ἐπιγνώσει τοῦ κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, “through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ” — ἐπίγνωσις, from the know family, as in 1:2–3. τούτοις δὲ πάλιν ἐμπλακέντες ἡττῶνται, “they are again entangled in it and overcome” — ἐμπλέκω, to weave in, entangle. γέγονεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ἔσχατα χείρονα τῶν πρώτων, “the last state has become worse for them than the first” — Jesus' own words (Matthew 12:45).

scripture.text: For it would be better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them.
scripture.understanding: κρεῖττον γὰρ ἦν αὐτοῖς μὴ ἐπεγνωκέναι τὴν ὁδὸν τῆς δικαιοσύνης, “For it would be better for them not to have known the way of righteousness” — κρείττων, better; ἐπιγινώσκω, from the know family, the verb of ἐπίγνωσις. ἢ ἐπιγνοῦσιν ὑποστρέψαι ἐκ τῆς παραδοθείσης αὐτοῖς ἁγίας ἐντολῆς, “than, after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them” — ἐντολή, the commandment; παραδίδωμι, handed down. Knowledge brings responsibility. Whether these were genuine believers who fell away or people who only tasted the truth without new birth is debated (compare Hebrews 6:4–6); verse 22 suggests their nature was never changed.

scripture.text: But it has happened to them according to the true proverb, “The dog turns to his own vomit again,” and “the sow that has washed to wallowing in the mire.”
scripture.understanding: συμβέβηκεν αὐτοῖς τὸ τῆς ἀληθοῦς παροιμίας, “But it has happened to them according to the true proverb” — παροιμία, a saying. “The dog turns to his own vomit again” — from Proverbs 26:11; ἐπιστρέφω, the ‘turn back’ of James 5:19–20, here turning the wrong way. “and the sow that has washed to wallowing in the mire” — λούω, to wash; κύλισμα, rolling; βόρβορος, mud. The dog and the pig were unclean animals; washing did not change their nature. These teachers cleaned up outwardly, but their hearts were never made new.

visualMeditations.title: Smuggled In
visualMeditations.image: Picture a city gate at dusk. Merchants pass through with carts of goods, and the guards check them casually. Hidden under bales of cloth in one cart is a sack of poison, smuggled in to be mixed into the city's food. The merchant smiles at the guards, speaks smoothly, and is waved through.
visualMeditations.meaning: “But false prophets also arose among the people, as false teachers will also be among you, who will secretly bring in destructive heresies, denying even the Master who bought them, bringing on themselves swift destruction” (v. 1). False teaching rarely announces itself. It comes in alongside true things, wrapped in smooth words, driven by greed (v. 3). The church must be alert at its gates.

visualMeditations.title: Rescued from the Fire
visualMeditations.image: Picture a city burning under a sky raining fire. Smoke billows over the plain; buildings collapse. On a road leading away, two angels are pulling a man, his wife and his daughters by the hand, hurrying them towards the hills. Behind them the city is turning to ash.
visualMeditations.meaning: God did not spare the angels who sinned, the world of Noah's day or Sodom and Gomorrah — but He preserved Noah and “delivered righteous Lot” (v. 7). “the Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment” (v. 9). Whatever corruption surrounds you, God knows how to rescue you.

visualMeditations.title: Wells Without Water
visualMeditations.image: Picture a traveller crossing a desert, his water skin empty. He sees a well ahead and runs to it, lowers the bucket, and pulls it up — dry. Above him, dark clouds gather, and his heart leaps at the promise of rain; but a gust of wind sweeps them away and the sky is empty again.
visualMeditations.meaning: “These are wells without water, clouds driven by a storm; for whom the blackness of darkness has been reserved forever” (v. 17). False teachers promise refreshment and freedom: “promising them liberty, while they themselves are bondservants of corruption” (v. 19). Test every teacher by whether they lead you to the living water of Christ or leave you thirsty and enslaved.

visualMeditations.title: The Washed Pig
visualMeditations.image: Picture a farmer who scrubs his pig clean, every bristle washed. He turns his back for a moment, and the pig trots straight to the muddiest corner of the yard and rolls in it with delight. Nearby, a dog that has been sick returns to sniff and eat what it brought up.
visualMeditations.meaning: “But it has happened to them according to the true proverb, ‘The dog turns to his own vomit again,’ and ‘the sow that has washed to wallowing in the mire’” (v. 22). Outward cleaning does not change an inward nature. Only new birth — becoming partakers of the divine nature (1:4) — makes a person hate the mud they once loved.

structure.label: False Teachers Will Come (v. 1-3)
structure.body: As false prophets arose in Israel, false teachers will arise in the church, secretly bringing in destructive heresies, denying the Master who bought them; many will follow their sensuality, the way of truth will be slandered, and in greed they will exploit believers with fabricated words; their judgement is not idle.

structure.label: God Judges and Rescues (v. 4-10a)
structure.body: If God judged the sinning angels, the ancient world and Sodom and Gomorrah, but preserved Noah and rescued righteous Lot, then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trials and to keep the unrighteous for judgement, especially those who indulge the flesh and despise authority.

structure.label: Their Character Exposed (v. 10b-16)
structure.body: They are bold and arrogant, slandering glorious beings that even angels do not accuse; like unreasoning animals they will be destroyed; they revel in daylight, are blots at the church's feasts, have eyes full of adultery, entice unstable souls, are trained in greed, and follow the way of Balaam, who loved the wages of wrongdoing and was rebuked by a donkey.

structure.label: Empty Promises and Final Ruin (v. 17-22)
structure.body: They are waterless springs and wind-driven mists, uttering empty boasts and enticing new converts with promises of freedom while they themselves are slaves of corruption; those who escape the world through knowing Christ and are then entangled again are worse off than before, like a dog returning to its vomit or a washed pig to the mud.

sections.heading: Wolves Inside the Fold
paragraphs: Chapter 1 ended with true prophets carried along by the Holy Spirit. Chapter 2 begins with their opposites: “But false prophets also arose among the people, as false teachers will also be among you” (v. 1). Jesus warned, “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves” (Matthew 7:15). Paul told the Ephesian elders, “Men will arise from among your own selves, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them” (Acts 20:30). The danger is not only from outside; it grows inside the church.

Peter describes their method and motive. Their method is stealth: they “secretly bring in destructive heresies” (v. 1), mixing poison into wholesome food. Their message denies “the Master who bought them” — not necessarily in words, but in lives that reject His lordship. Their morality is sensual, and “Many will follow their immoral ways” (v. 2). And their motive is greed: “In covetousness they will exploit you with deceptive words” (v. 3). Religion becomes a business; believers become customers.

This chapter closely parallels Jude 4–18, which uses many of the same examples and images. Whether Peter used Jude, Jude used Peter, or both drew on common teaching is debated; what matters is that two apostolic voices give the same warning. The church in every age needs it, because the same pattern repeats: smooth words, a gospel without holiness, and leaders who serve their appetites rather than Christ.

sections.heading: God Knows How to Rescue and How to Judge
paragraphs: In the middle of the warnings, Peter builds one long sentence (vv. 4–9) on three examples from Genesis. God did not spare the angels who sinned but cast them into Tartarus to await judgement. He did not spare the ancient world but brought the flood — yet preserved Noah, “a preacher of righteousness” (v. 5). He reduced Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes — yet rescued Lot, “very distressed by the lustful life of the wicked” (v. 7).

The conclusion is the heart of the chapter: “the Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment” (v. 9). This is comfort for faithful believers surrounded by corruption, as Lot was. Lot was not perfect — Genesis shows his weakness — but he was tormented daily by the evil he saw and heard (v. 8). God saw that grief and rescued him. Jesus pointed to the same events: “Likewise, even as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built” (Luke 17:28), “but in the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from the sky, and destroyed them all” (Luke 17:29).

It is also a warning. God's patience with false teachers is not indifference: “whose sentence now from of old doesn’t linger, and their destruction will not slumber” (v. 3). The same God who judged angels, the world and cities will judge those who lead His people astray.

sections.heading: The Anatomy of False Teaching
paragraphs: Peter's portrait of the false teachers is vivid and harsh, in the style of the Old Testament prophets. They despise authority and slander spiritual powers that even angels treat with caution (vv. 10–11). They live like unreasoning animals, driven by instinct (v. 12). They party in broad daylight and sit at the church's love feasts as ‘spots and defects’ (v. 13) — the opposite of Christ, the spotless Lamb. Their eyes are “full of adultery”, their hearts “trained in greed” (v. 14). They follow Balaam, the prophet who loved money more than God (v. 15), and who was rebuked by his own donkey (v. 16).

Their offer is freedom: “promising them liberty, while they themselves are bondservants of corruption; for a man is brought into bondage by whoever overcomes him” (v. 19). This is the oldest lie: that freedom means having no restraint. Jesus said, “Most certainly I tell you, everyone who commits sin is the bondservant of sin” (John 8:34). Paul: “Don’t you know that when you present yourselves as servants and obey someone, you are the servants of whomever you obey” (Romans 6:16). True freedom is the freedom to obey God.

The chapter ends with a terrible verdict: those who escape the world's defilement through knowing Christ, and are then entangled again, end worse than before (vv. 20–21). The strongest reading of verse 22 is that these people never truly changed: like the washed pig and the dog, their nature remained the same, and they went back to what they were. John says the same of those who left the church: “They went out from us, but they didn’t belong to us” (1 John 2:19). But the warning is real for everyone: outward religion without inward new birth will not last.

ntConnection.heading: False Prophets, Balaam and the Last State
paragraphs: Jesus predicted exactly what Peter describes: “For there will arise false christs, and false prophets, and they will show great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones” (Matthew 24:24). And His words about the unclean spirit returning stand behind verse 20: “The last state of that man becomes worse than the first. Even so will it be also to this evil generation” (Matthew 12:45).

Jude gives a parallel warning: “For there are certain men who crept in secretly, even those who were long ago written about for this condemnation: ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into indecency, and denying our only Master, God, and Lord, Jesus Christ” (Jude 1:4). He too names Balaam: “Woe to them! For they went in the way of Cain, and ran riotously in the error of Balaam for hire” (Jude 1:11). And the risen Christ warned the church at Pergamum about “some who hold the teaching of Balaam” (Revelation 2:14).

The ‘Master who bought them’ (v. 1) recalls Paul: “for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s” (1 Corinthians 6:20), and heaven's song: “you were killed, and bought us for God with your blood” (Revelation 5:9). Those who have truly been bought glorify their Master; false teachers deny Him.

lexicon.strongs: G139 (secretly bring in παρεισάγω, pareiságō, G3919)
lexicon.insight: Strong's: “properly, a choice, i.e. (specially) a party or (abstractly) disunion.” αἵρεσις first meant a choice, then a school of thought or party (the ‘sect’ of the Pharisees, Acts 15:5). In Christian use it came to mean teaching chosen in opposition to the apostolic gospel. Paul lists it among the works of the flesh (Galatians 5:20). Peter calls these heresies ‘of destruction’ — they ruin those who believe them — and says they are smuggled in, mixed with truth so as to pass unnoticed.

Strong's: “to incarcerate in eternal torment.” ταρταρόω is used only here in the Bible. In Greek mythology Tartarus was the deepest pit beneath Hades, where the rebel Titans were imprisoned. Peter borrows the word his readers knew to describe the prison of the angels who sinned, held until the judgement. Jude speaks of the same angels ‘kept in everlasting bonds under darkness’. The point is not mythology but certainty: if God judged rebellious angels, He will judge false teachers.

Strong's: “to watch, i.e. be on guard (literally or figuratively).” φυλάσσω and τηρέω are both in the hold family, and Peter uses both in this passage with opposite effects. τηρέω (vv. 4, 9, 17) is used of the wicked being ‘kept’ for judgement; φυλάσσω (v. 5) of Noah being ‘guarded’ for life. God watches over both, with different ends. In 3:17 Peter uses φυλάσσω again: ‘beware’ — guard yourselves.

Strong's: “to practise naked (in the games), i.e. train (figuratively).” γυμνάζω gives us ‘gymnasium’. It belongs to the discipline family: Hebrews 12:11 uses it of believers trained by God's discipline, and 1 Timothy 4:7 of training oneself in godliness. Peter turns it upside down: the false teachers have trained their hearts — in greed. Every heart is being trained in something. The question is whether you are exercising yourself in godliness or in desire.

lexicon.strongs: G1402 (bondservants δοῦλος, doûlos, G1401; overcomes ἡττάω, hēttáō, G2274)
lexicon.insight: Strong's: “to enslave (literally or figuratively).” δουλόω and δοῦλος, from the servant family, describe the false teachers' real condition: they promise freedom but are slaves of φθορά, corruption. ἡττάω means to be defeated, to lose a fight. Peter's principle is universal: whatever defeats you owns you. Believers are also δοῦλοι — of God (1 Peter 2:16) — and that is the only slavery that sets anyone free.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this chapter the Holy Spirit is sharpening your discernment and assuring you of His protection in a corrupt world.

items.title: Test the Teachers
items.body: Not everyone who speaks about God speaks for God. The Spirit asks you to test the voices you listen to: Do they exalt Christ as Lord and Master? Do they call for holiness, or excuse sin as freedom? Are they generous servants, or do they treat people as merchandise (v. 3)? Is their life consistent with their words? Ask Him for discernment about one voice you have been trusting.

items.title: Grieved Like Lot
items.body: Lot was “tormented in his righteous soul from day to day with seeing and hearing lawless deeds” (v. 8). Does the evil around you still grieve you, or have you grown used to it? The Spirit wants to keep your conscience tender. Ask Him to restore your grief over sin — and to remind you that “the Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation” (v. 9).

items.title: What Owns You?
items.body: “for a man is brought into bondage by whoever overcomes him” (v. 19). Is there a habit, appetite or desire that regularly defeats you? Whatever defeats you owns you. The Spirit does not condemn you; He offers freedom in Christ. Name it before Him and ask for the power of the divine nature (1:4) to break its grip.

audit.title: The Voice Check
audit.body: List the teachers, preachers, writers and online voices you regularly listen to. Measure each by verses 1–3 and 18–19: Do they honour Christ's lordship, call to holiness, and serve rather than exploit?

audit.title: The Grief Check
audit.body: What evil in your culture or entertainment no longer bothers you (v. 8)? What has dulled your conscience?

audit.title: The Freedom Check
audit.body: Is there anything you call ‘freedom’ that is actually bondage (v. 19)? Is there an old sin you have been tempted to return to (v. 22)?

practices.title: A Discernment Grid
practices.body: Write four questions on a card: (1) Does this teaching exalt Jesus as Lord and Saviour? (2) Does it agree with the plain teaching of Scripture? (3) Does it lead to holiness and love, or excuse sin? (4) Does the teacher's life and use of money match the message? Use the card this month with every new teaching, video or book you encounter.

practices.title: Break One Chain
practices.body: Identify one area where you are being overcome (v. 19). This week, confess it to God and to a trusted believer, remove one access point to it, and memorise 1:3–4. Each time temptation comes, say aloud: ‘His divine power has given me everything I need for godliness. I am not a slave of corruption.’

prayerReflection: “Lord Jesus, my Master who bought me with Your blood, I confess You as Lord. Guard me and Your church from false teachers who secretly bring in destructive heresies, who deny You with their lives and exploit Your people with smooth words. Give me discernment to recognise wells without water and clouds without rain. Thank You that You know how to rescue the godly from trials, as You preserved Noah and rescued righteous Lot. Keep my heart tender, grieved by the evil I see and hear, not hardened by it. Do not let me be enticed by promises of a freedom that is really slavery. Whatever has been overcoming me, break its power, because I belong to You. Keep me from returning to what You washed me from. Train my heart, not in greed or desire, but in godliness. And let me never deny You, my Master, in word or in life. In Your name, Amen.”

storyConnections.title: Lot in Sodom
storyConnections.summary: Lot had chosen to live near Sodom for its rich pasture, and in time he settled inside the city. When two angels came to warn him of judgement, the men of the city surrounded his house with violent intent. The angels struck them blind and urged Lot to flee with his family. He hesitated, and the angels seized his hand and his family's hands and brought them out, ‘Yahweh being merciful to him’. Then fire and sulphur fell, and the cities were destroyed. Lot's choices were not wise, but Peter calls him righteous and grieved by the evil around him — and God rescued him.

storyConnections.title: Balaam and the Donkey
storyConnections.summary: Balak, king of Moab, offered the prophet Balaam rich rewards to curse Israel. God told Balaam not to go, but the money drew him. As he rode, the angel of the Lord stood in the road with a drawn sword. The donkey saw the angel and turned aside three times; Balaam beat her each time. Then the Lord opened the donkey's mouth, and she asked why he was beating her. Balaam's eyes were opened, and he saw the angel. Later he advised Moab to lead Israel into idolatry and immorality. Peter uses him as the pattern of the false teacher: a religious man for hire, who loved the wages of wrongdoing.

storyConnections.title: Noah, the Preacher of Righteousness
storyConnections.summary: In a world filled with violence, Noah walked with God. While he built the ark for many years, he became, as Peter calls him, ‘a preacher of righteousness’ — his words and his work warned his generation. No one but his family listened. When the flood came, God shut them in and preserved them. Hebrews says, “By faith, Noah, being warned about things not yet seen, moved with godly fear, prepared a ship for the saving of his house, through which he condemned the world” (Hebrews 11:7). Noah is proof that one faithful family can stand in a corrupt world, and that God guards those who are His.
